title: Hipparcos and TESS eclipse depths agree for 122 of 128 single detached binaries over 30 years; no outlier is an orbital change, and the apparent new eclipse of HD 210055 is a sampling gap
abstract: Turning orbital planes change eclipse depths and show third bodies, as in HD 93683 and HD 303514. We tested how often this occurs over 30 years. We fitted TESS (2018-2026) eclipse templates to Hipparcos epoch photometry (1989.9-1993.2) of 1,857 Hipparcos stars: all SIMBAD eclipsing binaries with HIP numbers and 402 more from the Prsa et al. (2022) TESS catalogue. Most TESS templates are QLP full-frame light curves. Of 196 measurable detached binaries (128 single in Hipparcos), 122 single stars show Hipparcos eclipses whose depths agree with TESS (median ratio 1.03, 16-84 percent range 0.92-1.19) inside a blackbody band tolerance and a 13.6 percent systematic floor from near-twin binaries. None of the six single-star outliers is an orbital change: two Hipparcos phase-coverage gaps, one star too faint in eclipse, one timing change with poor coverage, one spotted binary and one W Ser binary. The known eclipse loss of HS Hya is recovered. With the 79 binaries of SCI e1b375b4 (68 of ours are new), 147 single detached binaries limit factor-of-2 changes to below 2.0 percent (95 percent; 3.2 percent with one unresolved case). HD 210055 first looked like a new eclipse after 1993 (17.6 percent deep in TESS, none in Hipparcos). At the ephemeris from ASAS-3, Gaia DR3 and TESS, no Hipparcos epoch falls in the eclipse, and ASAS-3 (2000-2009), Gaia (2014-2017) and SPOC (2018-2026) show a constant depth. Its eclipse times move by 16 min and Gaia RUWE is 4.35, so a third body is possible. QLP depths of bright binaries (Tmag 2.2-5.9) are 1.11 times SPOC depths with 0.13 scatter. Limits: few measurable systems, QLP depth errors, approximate band model, rules partly set after first inspection, and no orbit fit for HD 210055.
